transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
President Trump has changed his mind again
and will now hold rallies Sunday in Kansas and Iowa.
As NPR's Frank Ordonez reports,
Trump says Republican officials asked him to reconsider his decision to cancel.
The president had said earlier that he was canceling those visits
because Republicans were in good shape in those states.
But now he's taking a different tack.
We got a call from Iowa and from the people
and from my friends that are very, very good.
And we have a couple of races that are very important.
And they said if you could go, it would be better than a teller rally.
And I tried to talk about that.
I said, "What about a teller rally?"
But they asked me, "So I'm going to do two on Sunday."
The president says he's not going on Saturday because of college football,
but would leave early Sunday morning for Iowa and then head to Kansas.
Franko Ordonez, NPR News, The White House.
Food security and energy top the agenda.
As Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with his counterparts
from the Group of 20 on Friday,
Poland is lobbying to join the group over objections from Russia.
As NPR's Michelle Kellerman reports,
Poland has faced cyberattacks and other provocations from Russia
during the ongoing war with Ukraine.
Polish Foreign Minister Radek Sikorski says he was glad to be sitting right next to Rubio
and he used his remarks to push for a ceasefire in the Black Sea
to allow grain shipments from both Ukraine and Russia.
I spoke in favor of doing something quickly
because the people of the global south need this grain.
Russia's foreign minister complained about Poland being invited to the G20 meeting.
Sikorski says he had positive meetings with other members
as he lobbies for Poland to join.
And he says if Russia wants to export its energy again to Europe,
there has to be a "fair end" to the war of aggression against Ukraine.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, Atlanta.
The tech sell-off is deepening on Wall Street.
The Nasdaq closed on Friday with its worst month in over a year.
NPR's Stephen Besaha reports that investors are now questioning
if the massive spending on AI is still worth the price.
These stock drops look even steeper when you zoom out to the past month.
Facebook's parent company, Meta, is down more than 15 percent.
Google's parent company, Alphabet, down more than 18 percent.
Intel down more than 45 percent.
This sell-off sped up as tech companies updated investors
about the massive amounts of money they are spending on AI,
particularly on data centers.
That's given investors sticker shock.
Other parts of the market are also feeling the sting of high oil prices.
Crude oil futures are up, selling at more than $104 a barrel.
Stephen Besaha, NPR News.
And again, stocks were down across the board on Friday.
You're listening to NPR News.
A parade celebrating Milwaukee's first Major League Baseball Championship
in 69 years brought tens of thousands of people to the city's downtown on Friday.
Chuck Kornbach was there and filed our reports.
The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays in the World Series this week.
Brewers fans at the parade cheered their heroes on
as the players went by on platforms atop buses.
Forty-three-year-old Alvaro Aleman says he just had to be on hand.
Oh my God, I've been waiting for this my entire life.
I've been waiting for this my entire life to see World Series champions.
It's the Brewers' first championship joining the Milwaukee Braves
who won the World Series in 1957.
For NPR News, I'm Chuck Kornbach in Milwaukee.
An ICE officer accused of intentionally ramming his car
into a Mexican construction worker in Houston
has been charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.
Prosecutors say Mario Alberto Morales was driving an unmarked SUV
when it hit 48-year-old Miguel Parra Hernandez.
ICE claims Parra Hernandez ran out in front of the car,
but prosecutors say that video evidence shows that he was running away.
Christa Pike says she lives in pain following a botched execution attempt in Tennessee last month.
She was given two lethal injections that put her in the hospital but did not kill her.
In her first public statement Friday, she said she was deeply hurt by the incompetence
and she thanked the medical workers who saved her.
Pike says she went to the execution chamber prepared to die in peace
but instead woke up confused in a hospital bed.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump reverses course, will hold Sunday rallies in Iowa and Kansas after GOP requests
Poland lobbies to join G20 as Rubio meets counterparts; Sikorski urges Black Sea grain ceasefire
Tech stock sell-off deepens as Nasdaq posts worst month in over a year on AI spending doubts
Milwaukee Brewers fans celebrate first MLB championship in 69 years with downtown parade
ICE officer charged with aggravated assault for allegedly ramming Houston construction worker Miguel Parra Hernandez
Christa Pike speaks publicly on pain after botched Tennessee execution attempt last month
